s1.syndrome_frame: A toddler with a chronic skin eruption characterized by multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale, accompanied by fever and otitis media
salient_findings: Multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale
Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm on histopathology
Scattered café au lait macules present on the back
key_facts: The eruption began 2 months previously
The patient has a medical history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and juvenile xanthogranulomas
Treatment with griseofulvin and clotrimazole had not improved the rash
The patient developed fever and was diagnosed with otitis media one day prior to presentation
Current medications included acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and amoxicillin
No family history of NF1
White blood cell count: 76,400/µL
Histopathology showed perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm
Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate with positive CD4 and CD163 immunohistochemical staining

shortlist.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's medical history and presence of café au lait macules

shortlist.label: Leukemia cutis
shortlist.why_kept: High white blood cell count and perivascular infiltrate

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Annular, indurated plaques with central clearing and trailing scale

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate with positive CD4 and CD163 immunohistochemical staining

raw.rationale: The patient's high white blood cell count (76,400/µL) and the histopathology showing perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, along with positive immunohistochemical staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163, are more indicative of leukemia cutis, especially given the lack of improvement with antifungal treatment and the presence of systemic symptoms like fever and otitis media.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Negative staining for CD1a and S100, which are typically positive in Langerhans cell histiocytosis

rejected.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The patient already has a history of juvenile xanthogranuloma, but the current presentation and histopathology do not match this diagnosis

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathology do not align with lymphomatoid papulosis, which typically shows a CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell infiltrate

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: The immunohistochemical staining pattern does not support Rosai-Dorfman disease, which typically shows positive staining for S100 and CD68
